provenance: Synthetic demo procedure; not a manufacturer instruction
text: Falling delivered flow with a changed pressure profile may be consistent with internal pump leakage, valve bypass, or operating-load changes. Compare flow, pressure, motor power, and operating conditions before assigning a cause. A condition label from a test rig does not establish time to failure.

provenance: Synthetic demo procedure; not a manufacturer instruction
text: A single extreme pressure reading while independent flow, power, and temperature remain normal is insufficient to confirm mechanical failure. Request an independent pressure measurement and sensor calibration check. Do not infer a safe operating condition solely from disagreement.

provenance: Synthetic demo procedure; not a manufacturer instruction
text: An authorized human must approve the intervention before a work order is issued. A technician records the observed cause, fix, and parts. Work completion is not proof of recovery. Verify three consecutive healthy telemetry windows before storing a confirmed case. Actual plant isolation procedures require site-specific review.

Trace the incident asset through the directed dependencies in the incident's versioned plant model. Count each affected production area once, even when paths converge at dispatch. Use configured line capacities rather than assuming a fixed number of lines or fraction of whole-plant output. Equipment outside the affected dependency paths is not automatically stopped; shared utilities can constrain multiple lines.

source: UCI Machine Learning Repository - hydraulic condition dataset
provenance: Public CC BY 4.0 dataset metadata; paraphrased; https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/447/condition+monitoring+of+hydraulic+systems
text: The hydraulic test rig repeats 60-second load cycles. Its pressure, volume-flow, temperature, motor-power and vibration measurements accompany cycle-level component conditions. The pump target distinguishes no internal leakage, weak leakage and severe leakage. Cooler, valve and accumulator conditions also vary. Multiple faults can coexist, so a pressure or flow change alone does not uniquely establish a pump cause. Test-rig condition labels do not provide calibrated future failure probabilities.

provenance: Synthetic demo procedure; not a manufacturer instruction
text: Reduced cooling performance may be consistent with fouling, low cooling flow, excess heat load or temperature instrumentation. Compare cooling efficiency, cooling power, temperature and flow; independently inspect the shared circuit. Trace the incident's versioned dependency graph to identify every line supplied by the cooling unit.

provenance: Synthetic demo procedure; not a manufacturer instruction
text: Valve timing degradation may change pressure distributions and cycle flow. Cycle means alone may hide timing faults. Compare pressure and flow variation and independently measure spool response before attributing a press problem to the valve.

provenance: Synthetic demo procedure; not a manufacturer instruction
text: Elevated acceleration RMS, impulsiveness or spectral changes may be consistent with bearing damage, looseness, misalignment or acquisition differences. Acceleration is not velocity. Inspect the bearing and alignment independently; test-rig or synthetic demonstration signals cannot confirm damage in a real plant.

source: NASA IMS bearing archive / bundled dataset README
provenance: Public dataset metadata; https://data.nasa.gov/dataset/ims-bearings; supplied by University of Cincinnati IMS with Rexnord support
text: The second experiment has four channels and 984 snapshots; channel one corresponds to bearing one. Snapshots contain 20,480 samples acquired at 20 kHz. The README reports outer-race failure of bearing one at the experiment endpoint. It does not label every snapshot with a fault or specify amplitude units. Retain source units and distinguish an early/late replay demonstration from validated industrial diagnosis or an observed repair.
